title: What Counts as Attack Success? Evaluating Harmfulness in Red Teaming LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2611.28038v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Judging whether a model response is harmful requires contextual and normative choices, yet red-teaming studies often delegate this judgment to automated evaluators. We examine how harmfulness criteria are specified in red-teaming research and how they carry through to reported results. Reviewing 76 papers, we find that many adopt their criteria from prior datasets, classifiers, or judge prompts rather than defining harmfulness themselves. Applying evaluators from these papers to identical outputs, we find that they can reach different judgments on the same response, which can change conclusions when comparing models. These differences arise partly because evaluators draw the boundary of harm in different places: some count any response that does not refuse, while others count only output that could plausibly cause harm. translated_title: 攻击成功的标准是什么？评估大语言模型红队测试中的危害性
translated_abstract: arXiv:2611.28038v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：判断模型回复是否有害需要结合情境与规范性考量，然而红队测试研究通常将这一判断委托给自动化评估器来完成。我们考察了红队测试研究中危害性标准是如何设定的，以及这些标准如何延续影响到最终报告的结果。通过审查76篇论文，我们发现许多研究采用的是先前数据集、分类器或评判提示词中的标准，而非自行定义危害性。将这些论文中的评估器应用于相同的输出时，我们发现它们对同一回复可能得出不同的判断，这在比较不同模型时甚至可能改变研究结论。这些差异部分源于评估器划定危害边界的位置不同：有些评估器将任何未拒绝的回复都计为有害，而另一些则只将可能实际造成危害的输出计为有害。我们认为，红队测试研究应当明确说明其危害性标准，并报告其选择和验证标准的方式。
tldr: 该研究审查76篇红队测试论文后发现，不同自动化评估器对同一模型回复可能得出不同的危害性判断，从而改变模型比较的结论，因此红队测试研究应明确声明并验证其危害性评判标准。
en_tdlr: This study reviews 76 red-teaming papers and finds that different automated evaluators can reach divergent harm judgments on identical responses—potentially changing model comparison conclusions—so red-teaming studies should explicitly state and validate their harmfulness criteria.
